anxiety_info.title: Why do we feel anxious?
anxiety_info.description: Anxiety isn't an enemy trying to hurt us—it's a signal from the heart to keep us safe.

step1.title: Anxiety is a survival alarm
content: Since ancient times, anxiety has been a helpful alarm protecting us from danger.
It's an instinctive signal from the brain shouting, "Be careful!"
So feeling anxious means your survival instinct is working perfectly and healthily.

step2.title: It rolls in and fades like waves
content: Anxiety doesn't stay in our hearts forever.
Like waves in the ocean, it slowly rises, peaks, and gently subsides again.
This anxiety may feel like it will last forever, but remember—every wave is bound to pass.

step3.title: The more you block it, the bigger it gets
content: What happens if you try to block a rushing wave with your bare body?
You'll likely feel a greater impact or get swept away more easily.
Anxiety is the same. The more you resist, the more fiercely it crashes over your surface.

step4.title: Soothe your sensitive alarm
content: In modern life, the alarm often rings even when there's no real danger.
Instead of trying to break the alarm, it's important to acknowledge its state first.
Gently say to yourself, "The alarm is ringing right now. I'm feeling tense."

step5.title: Moving forward with anxiety
content: You don't have to get rid of anxiety entirely to be happy.
Just as the deep current doesn't lose its way even when surface waves are high,
we can move toward the life we want while holding our anxiety within.

act_guide.title: Moving Forward with Anxiety
act_guide.description: Instead of fighting anxiety, let's learn about ACT—a way to move toward the life you want, even when you feel anxious.

step1.title: What is ACT?
content: ACT (Acceptance and Commitment Therapy) helps you accept anxiety as it is,
rather than suppressing it, and commit to acting toward the values you hold dear.
Our app breaks this process into 5 steps you can easily follow.

step2.title: Rising to the surface of the present
content: When caught in a whirlpool of thoughts, try Step 1 (Grounding) and Step 2 (Emotion Diary).
By focusing on your senses and calmly recording the weather of your heart,
you can find your own calm deep sea that stays centered amidst the rough waves.

step3.title: Separating thoughts from facts
content: Step 3 (Separating Thoughts from Facts) helps you see thoughts like "I will fail" objectively.
It's a practice of isolating just the 'thought'—the wind—from the rest of the sentence.
Remember, thoughts are merely wind brushing across the surface, not absolute facts of the ocean.

step4.title: Flowing with the rhythm of the waves
content: In Step 4 (Expanding the Sea Within), breathe along with the rising and falling wave animation.
Instead of pushing anxiety away, make space within your deep sea for it to simply stay.
As you breathe in and out, let the wave of anxiety just flow through you.

step5.title: Moving toward my own values
content: In the final step, discover the values you truly cherish and take action.
Even if you feel anxious, you can still take small steps toward your values.
Holding your anxiety within, start with a small action you can take today.
